name: Free Claude Code
cost: Free and open source (AGPL-3.0). Free tiers are set by each provider; paid providers bill you
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Cline, Hermes, DeepSeek Harness, Grok Build, Muse Code, Aider and VS Code Chat
short: A local proxy that lets 11 coding agents use models from 61 providers, including free tiers and local models, from one admin page.
what: Free Claude Code (FCC) runs a local server with an Admin UI where you add provider keys and pick models. Launchers like `fcc-claude` and `fcc-codex` start your coding agent pointed at it. If a model fails after retries, FCC tries the next model on your fallback list. It can also connect editors and apps, run Codex sessions in the browser, and take requests from Discord or Telegram.
who: Developers who want to run their coding agent on other or cheaper models, mix providers, or use local models through Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp. Skip it if you're happy with the single provider your agent ships with.
needs: At least one coding agent, chosen during install
At least one provider key. The quick start uses a free NVIDIA NIM key from build.nvidia.com
Or a local model server: Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp

steps.title: Install on macOS or Linux
steps.text: When prompted, choose at least one coding agent. You can also turn on RTK and Headroom to cut token use.

steps.title: Start FCC
steps.text: On Windows and macOS, open Free Claude Code from the desktop or the Start menu or Applications folder. On Linux run this and keep the terminal open. The Admin UI opens after it starts.

steps.title: Add a provider key
steps.text: Create a key at build.nvidia.com/settings/api-keys. In the Admin UI open NVIDIA NIM in Providers, click Add key, paste it and click Save. Keep the default model or pick another, then click Apply.

steps.title: Run your coding agent
steps.text: Each agent has its own launcher, such as `fcc-codex`, `fcc-pi`, `fcc-opencode` or `fcc-aider`.

steps.title: Update or troubleshoot
steps.text: Stop all running FCC commands before updating. `fcc-doctor` prints details for a bug report.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `fcc-claude`, then open the `/model` picker and select one of your FCC models.

watch: The README tells you to pipe the installer straight into a shell. Read `install.sh` or `install.ps1` first.
It's an independent project. The README says it isn't affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.
Free-tier availability and limits are set by each provider and can change.
With fallback models on, one failed request may reach and use up quota from more than one provider before it succeeds.
FCC runs a local proxy. Turn on Proxy Authentication in Admin if you want it protected with a bearer token.
Some providers connect your own subscription accounts (ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot). Kimi Code and QwenCloud Coding Plan keys are for personal interactive coding use under their own terms.
The Discord and Telegram bots work on an Allowed Directory you set. Give them a narrow folder.
Licensed AGPL-3.0, which matters if you plan to modify it and offer it to others over a network.
